eyebrow: Lesson 12 · B1 · Good Manners in Public · 20 câu
heading: Small Kindnesses
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners in Public – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 16–21.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners in Public (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: You've just found a great seat by the door on a bus. Before you get comfortable, look around. Is there someone who needs that seat more than you? A {pregnant|pregnant} woman may have {sore|sore} feet, and an older person may find it hard to stand while the bus is moving. {Offer|offer} your seat by standing up and asking, "Would you like to sit down?"

paras.label: B
paras.text: Little words can make a big difference. When someone holds a door open for you, remember to say "Thank you!" If you {bump into|bump into} someone {by accident|by accident}, say "Excuse me" or "Sorry" so they know you didn't mean it. A quick {apology|apology} can {turn a frown upside down|turn a frown upside down}.

paras.label: C
paras.text: When someone wishes you a nice day, reply, "Thanks, you too!" A simple thank-you can make another person's day much brighter.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Remember that public spaces {belong to|belong to} everyone: every person in the world, and the animals that share these places with us. Taking care of them is part of having good manners.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Good manners in public make life easier and more {pleasant|pleasant}. So take a shower, pick up your rubbish, {give up|give up} your seat, turn your music down and thank someone every day. Show respect to others, and they will show respect to you.

vocab.vi: biến cái nhăn mặt thành nụ cười

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that describes people who may need to sit down
items.why: Đoạn A: phụ nữ mang thai, người lớn tuổi.

items.label: A paragraph that explains how to show that something was an accident
A paragraph that tells you how to reply to a friendly wish
A paragraph that mentions animals using public spaces
items.why: Đoạn D: *the animals that share these places with us.*

items.label: A paragraph that gives a list summarising the advice
items.why: Đoạn E liệt kê: tắm, nhặt rác, nhường ghế…

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: Why might an older person need a seat on the bus?
options: It may be hard for them to stand while the bus moves.
They want to sit by the door.
They are going to a party.
They don't like standing near children.
questions.why: *an older person may find it hard to stand while the bus is moving.*

questions.q: The writer suggests waiting until people ask for your seat.
questions.why: Sai. Hãy chủ động *Offer your seat… asking, "Would you like to sit down?"*

questions.q: Why should you say "Sorry" after bumping into someone?
options: so they know you didn't do it on purpose
so they will give you their seat
questions.why: *so they know you didn't mean it.*

questions.q: According to paragraph D, who do public spaces belong to?
options: only the people who live nearby

questions.q: The writer believes that if you respect others, they will respect you too.
Which piece of advice is NOT in the list in paragraph E?
questions.why: Danh sách không có việc xách đồ giúp.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Which advice from the text is the boy following?
options: offering his seat to someone who needs it more
saying sorry after bumping into someone
questions.why: Đúng đoạn A: nhường ghế cho người lớn tuổi.
questions.alt: A boy stands up and asks an older woman with a walking stick: Would you like to sit down?

questions.q: According to paragraph B, why is saying "Thank you!" a good idea?
options: Little words can make a big difference.
It is the only polite word in English.
It means you want something else.
questions.why: *Little words can make a big difference.*
questions.alt: One boy puts his hand on another boy's shoulder and says Thank you!

questions.q: What should the two adults say to the boy?
questions.why: Đoạn B: khi được giữ cửa, nhớ nói *Thank you!*
questions.alt: A boy holds a door open for two adults with bags

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Yesterday I was hurrying to catch the bus when I bumped into a lady carrying shopping bags. [1] I stopped, said "I'm so sorry," and helped her pick everything up. [2] Then, on the bus, I gave my seat to an old man with a walking stick. [3]
options: Oranges rolled all over the pavement.
Her angry face turned into a big smile.
He thanked me so warmly that it made my whole day.
I kept running and didn't look back.
She told me I was a queue jumper.

items.why: Va vào người → cam lăn ra đường, dẫn đến việc *pick everything up*.
Lời xin lỗi *turn a frown upside down* – mặt giận thành nụ cười.
Nhường ghế → ông cảm ơn, làm mình vui cả ngày.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *If you bump into someone by accident…* (B). **By accident** means…
*A quick apology can turn a frown upside down* (B). This means it can…
questions.why: Lật ngược cái nhăn mặt → thành nụ cười.

questions.q: *…give up your seat* (E). Here, **give up** means…
